title: The 1958 perceptron was promised to walk and talk
body: Frank Rosenblatt's perceptron learned to classify images with adjustable weights, and the New York Times reported Navy expectations of machines that would walk, talk and be conscious. The gap between a trainable neuron and those promises set a hype pattern the field still repeats. Rosenblatt's maths was sound; the extrapolations were fundraising.
